top_strength: The booking mechanics were clean and fast, and the close was the best part of the call. She checked the calendar live and gave Jack a real answer ('twenty second Tuesday... it's currently wide open as we speak'), then anchored the price as a range rather than a single scary number — '$520 to 624' — and immediately paired it with 'there are no additional fees of any type. Literally just pay for the time that you use. By the way, we don't require any deposits. Are you ready to lock us in?' That is a well-built ask: value, no-risk, then the direct request, and Jack said yes on the spot. She also handled the referral question with genuine warmth ('Oh, good. Well, thank you to that friend'), which is a small touch worth keeping.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix, Amy: you sold on price alone and left every differentiator on the table. Jack booked because $520 sounded fine, not because he understood what he was buying — and a customer who bought on price will leave on price. After the rate, run the block every time: 'And Jack, a couple of things that come with every move — you get up to $2,000 in No Worries damage coverage, zero deductible, so if anything gets damaged we repair, replace or reimburse it. A few days before, you'll get an email with a photo of your actual movers so you know who is knocking. And we have an on-time guarantee — if we miss your arrival window we start discounting your bill immediately.' That is roughly forty seconds and it is the difference between a quote and a reason to choose Einstein. Second priority: the Save Your Ass speech, which mattered here more than usual because Jack told you he is moving solo with no help. He needed to hear 'the more prep you do before we arrive, the shorter the move and the lower the bill — get loose items into drawers and boxes, get the toys and the small stuff consolidated, and anything that fits in your car, take a carload over the day before. Does that make sense?' Third, and quick: you cut him off. He was mid-sentence on 'really I'm worried about' and you moved to pricing. Let the worry land and answer it — that is the one question on the call he actually asked you to answer. Also add the 10-15 minute timeframe to your opener; your roadmap and your 'does that sound good?' were both already there, so the timeframe alone would have earned the agenda credit.
